title: The Self Has Four Quarters
meter: Prose (the Upaniṣad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pāda and mātrā, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
iast: sarvaṃ hy etad brahmāyam ātmā brahma
translation: All this is indeed Brahman. This Self is Brahman. This Self has four quarters.
translation_hi: यह सब ब्रह्म ही है। यह आत्मा ब्रह्म है। यह आत्मा चार पादों वाला है।

words.note: catur + pād. pāda = foot, quarter: the same word as a quarter of a verse!

grammar: A great saying (mahāvākya): अयमात्मा ब्रह्म 'this Self is Brahman' is one of the four mahāvākyas of the Upaniṣads.
Pāda = quarter: the Self has four pādas just as an Anuṣṭubh verse has four pādas of eight syllables.
r → ṣ: चतुर् + पात् → चतुष्पात्. Before p, r becomes a visarga and then ṣ.
